input_signals.name: PayoutBackedOperatingProfit
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), sstk), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with persistently high industry-adjusted operating profitability that simultaneously return net capital to shareholders (repurchases plus dividends net of equity issuance) are generating cash the market underweights, and earn higher subsequent returns than equally profitable firms that are absorbing outside capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Smoothed operating profit over assets measures durable operating strength, while net payout over assets measures management's revealed confidence that internal cash exceeds investment needs. Ranking both channels and summing rewards the joint state (strong operations plus capital return) rather than either theme alone, and industry adjustment prevents the profitability leg from proxying for sector composition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_adj( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ratio( sub( add( prstkc, dvt ), sstk ), at ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitLessNetExternalFinanceRank
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, dvt))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose profitability is high relative to how much net external capital (new debt plus clean-surplus net equity issuance) they absorb are underpriced, because their earnings are self-financed rather than purchased with outside capital.
input_signals.reasoning: The clean-surplus construction ΔCEQ − (ib − dvt) infers net equity issuance from balance-sheet items and ΔDebt captures net borrowing, so the whole financing leg is available for nearly all firm-years, repairing the 0.08–0.12 coverage problem of generation 0. Differencing two industry ranks makes the signal an explicit contest between operating strength and external capital dependence rather than a profitability tilt with a small financing overlay.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_rank( ma( ratio( ib, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, dvt ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: WithinProfitableFinancingTilt
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), 0.5), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, dvt))), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Conditional on being an above-median profitability firm, those that shrink rather than expand their external capital base are underpriced; the financing signal carries information only when there is genuine operating cash to distribute.
input_signals.reasoning: The indicator restricts all non-zero signal values to profitable firms, so both the long and short extremes are drawn from the same profitability half and the RMW loading that destroyed generation 0's FF5 alpha largely cancels. Paired with Signal 1, this isolates a single design choice — gating versus rank differencing — on an identical, high-coverage financing measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, dvt ) ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashBackedEarningsVersusShareIssuance
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose reported earnings are backed by cash rather than accruals and that are simultaneously shrinking their share count are the highest-quality combination of operating strength and financing behavior, while accrual-heavy earnings accompanied by share issuance signal earnings management ahead of capital raising.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the profitability channel from level to *quality* (the accrual wedge ib − oancf) and the financing channel to share-count change, so the signal is not a restatement of the profitability-level family that FF5's RMW absorbs. Its economic content is that accruals must eventually be financed, making the accrual-issuance pairing informative beyond either component.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), neg( growth( csho, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: NetFinancingNewsAmongProfitableFirms
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: For cash-profitable firms, what matters is the change in *net* reliance on outside capital — issuance less repurchases, dividends and debt retirement — because gross issuance is often mere refinancing that carries no valuation information.
input_signals.reasoning: Generation 1's best FF5 alpha used the change in *gross* issuance, so this isolates one specific measurement choice: netting the financing flow against simultaneous distributions and repayments. A stronger result would show the effect is about a genuine swing from distributing to absorbing capital; a weaker result would tell us gross issuance events, not net flows, are what the market misprices.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualHeavyEquityIssuers
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0.7), WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose reported earnings are least cash-backed and that simultaneously expand their share count are managing earnings ahead of raising equity, and are the most overvalued corner of the profitability-financing space.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-1 composite of low accruals plus share shrinkage was strong (fmb 3.07, Sharpe 0.32) but symmetric, leaving open whether the information is in the good corner or the bad corner; gating on the top accrual tercile isolates the short leg where the economic story is sharpest. Because the gate uses earnings quality rather than earnings level, the resulting spread should be close to RMW-neutral.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), 0.7 ), winsor( growth( csho, 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitGrowthVersusDebtGrowth
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(GROWTH(oiadp, 1)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating profit is growing faster than their debt stock are expanding on internally generated funds and are underpriced, while firms whose borrowing outruns their profit growth are financing an unproven business with creditor capital.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the economic channel from levels or payout policy to a *growth-rate mismatch* between the operating engine and the balance sheet, which no archive signal tests, and it uses only high-coverage items so it should reach the top of the achievable coverage range. Because both legs are growth rates rather than levels, the spread should be less collinear with RMW and CMA than the gen-1 level-based composites that lost their alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_rank( growth( oiadp, 1 ) ), ind_rank( growth( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityChannelFinancingNewsAmongProfitable
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sstk, ADD(prstkc, dvt)), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: For cash-profitable firms the informative financing margin is the equity channel: a swing from returning cash to shareholders toward selling them new shares reveals that managers judge the stock rich, and predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates the equity half of the gen-2 winner by dropping debt issuance and repayment from the netting, testing whether the −3.8% alpha comes from shareholder-directed flows rather than creditor flows. If the alpha is preserved or improved, the mechanism is equity-market timing rather than general capital absorption.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( sstk, add( prstkc, dvt ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalFundingPerDollarOfEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), 0), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), MA(oibdp, 3)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically relevant quantity is external capital raised per dollar of operating earnings: a firm that must raise a year's worth of EBITDA from outside investors is far more dependent than one raising the same dollars against a much larger earnings base, and such dependence predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal scales financing by assets and treats profitability as a separate ranked leg, so the interaction is additive or gated; here profitability enters as the *deflator*, making the signal a true ratio interaction that cannot be decomposed into two main effects. The indicator on positive smoothed EBITDA keeps the denominator sign well defined, which is why earlier ratio ideas were avoided.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ), 0 ), winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), ma( oibdp, 3 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: TwoChannelRankBalancedFinancingNews
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sstk, ADD(prstkc, dvt)), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: For cash-profitable firms, a simultaneous swing toward creditor capital and toward shareholder capital is the strongest evidence of deteriorating self-funding, and the two channels should be weighted by cross-sectional rank rather than by raw dollars.
input_signals.reasoning: The decomposition showed the debt channel carries the FF5 alpha while the equity channel carries the Fama-MacBeth slope, so dollar-netting them inside one ratio lets whichever channel has larger dollar variance dominate; rank-balancing gives each channel equal influence and should lift both statistics at once. This directly targets the multi-metric objective rather than optimizing one statistic.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), ind_zscore( sumrank( delta( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ), 1 ), delta( ratio( sub( sstk, add( prstkc, dvt ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: NewBorrowingUnderHeavyInterestBurden
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(xint, oibdp)), 0.7), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cost of additional leverage depends on how much of operating profit is already pledged to lenders; firms in the top tercile of interest-to-EBITDA that borrow more are consuming their last financial flexibility and should underperform sharply.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests the financial-flexibility reading of the debt-news result by conditioning on debt-service burden — a profitability-relative quantity — instead of profitability level, and it predicts the effect concentrates where the earnings stream is least able to absorb new obligations. It is the mechanism-identifying counterpart to Signal 3's agency reading, so the pair discriminates between the two explanations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( xint, oibdp ) ), 0.7 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: FinancingDeviationFromOwnNorm
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 3)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: What is mispriced is a profitable firm's departure from its own habitual financing policy, not the level of that policy nor a single-year difference, because habitual issuers and habitual repurchasers are already understood by the market.
input_signals.reasoning: A one-year DELTA worked and a two-year DELTA did not, which suggests the informative object is a deviation from the firm's recent norm rather than a longer-horizon drift; benchmarking against the trailing three-year average keeps the timeliness of the one-year signal while filtering the transitory noise that a single difference inherits from the base year. This is a within-firm normalization, orthogonal to the cross-sectional normalizations tested so far.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), winsor( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), ma( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 3 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: FinancingIntensityAndNewsComposite
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), 0), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), MA(oibdp, 3)), 1), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm's dependence on outside capital has a persistent component, best measured as external funding per dollar of operating earnings, and a news component, best measured as the one-year change in financing intensity; both are mispriced and they carry complementary information.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's strongest Fama-MacBeth slope came from the earnings-deflated level (−3.98) and its strongest FF5 alpha from the asset-deflated one-year change (−3.07), and no signal has yet combined them, which is exactly what the multi-metric objective requires. Ranking the two legs before summing prevents the very wide-tailed earnings-deflated ratio from swamping the news leg in the extreme deciles.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ), 0 ), ind_zscore( sumrank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), ma( oibdp, 3 ) ), 1 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningsDeflatedFinancingNews
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), 0), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), MA(oibdp, 3)), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The swing toward external capital should be measured against the earnings stream that would otherwise fund the firm, so a change in external funding per dollar of EBITDA is a sharper statement of lost self-sufficiency than a change per dollar of assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Earnings deflation applied to the debt channel alone reached alpha −2.3% at 0.108 coverage, better coverage but weaker alpha than the asset-deflated full flow, leaving unresolved whether the loss came from the deflator or from restricting to debt; this tests the deflator with the full flow. Profitability entering as the denominator makes the interaction irreducible to two additive main effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ), 0 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), ma( oibdp, 3 ) ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: FinancingShockPerOwnVolatility
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), VOL(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 5)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: A given change in financing policy is surprising only relative to how variable that firm's financing has been; firms with habitually lumpy issuance generate large changes that convey little news, while a modest swing at a policy-stable profitable firm is highly informative.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal compares financing changes across firms in raw scaled units, so firms with volatile capital-market activity mechanically populate the extreme deciles and add noise to the spread; standardizing each firm's shock by its own five-year financing volatility converts the signal into a surprise measure. The cost is coverage from the five-year window, so this is an exploratory test of whether cleaner surprise identification is worth a narrower sample.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), winsor( ratio( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), vol( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitabilityWeightedFinancingNews
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The informativeness of a financing swing rises smoothly with the firm's cash profitability rather than switching on at the median, because the higher a firm's internal cash generation the less excusable is its turn to outside capital.
input_signals.reasoning: The hard indicator sets half the cross-section to exactly zero, which is the most likely reason the news family's Fama-MacBeth slopes sit near −2 despite strong alphas; replacing the gate with a continuous profitability-rank weight keeps the identical interaction economics while producing a signal defined and varying across the full sample. This tests whether the slope weakness is an estimation artifact of the mass point rather than an economic limitation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: FinancingNewsExcludingStickyDividends
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Dividends are deliberately smoothed and almost never change abruptly, so including them in the netted financing flow injects a slow-moving, already-anticipated component; the true news is in issuance, repurchase and debt repayment decisions.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a targeted measurement test on the winning construction: if removing the sticky dividend term raises the alpha t-stat, the effect is driven by discretionary capital-market transactions and future work should exclude dividends; if it weakens, the dividend commitment is genuinely part of the self-funding story. Coverage and structure are otherwise held fixed, so the comparison is clean.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: FinancingShockWhenEarningsArePredictable
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), 0.5), INDICATOR(NEG(IND_RANK(VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))), -0.5)), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: A financing surprise is only interpretable against a predictable earnings stream; when a profitable firm with stable, forecastable operating income suddenly reaches for outside capital, the market has no benign explanation and the negative information content is largest.
input_signals.reasoning: Every conditional so far gates on the level of profitability alone, whereas this adds a second-moment condition, testing whether earnings predictability is the missing ingredient that makes financing news informative rather than merely noisy. Low-volatility profitability was previously tested only as an additive rank leg in a payout composite, never as a conditioning state on financing news.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), indicator( neg( ind_rank( vol( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ) ) ), -0.5 ) ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: RepairedShockAgainstCashFlowNews
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), VOL(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 5)), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among cash-profitable firms the worst state joins two contemporaneous pieces of news — an unusual turn toward outside capital, measured against the firm's own financing habit, and a decline in internally generated cash — because together they identify a real breakdown of self-funding rather than a routine capital-markets transaction.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the repaired version of the generation-8 proposal lost to a syntax error, and it is the only combination of the archive's short-side alpha engine with its long-side alpha engine; both legs are news variables, so it avoids the generation-5 failure where a persistent level leg annihilated the alpha. Because the cash-flow-news leg already requires oancf, gating on cash profitability costs no coverage and uses the gate that historically produced the largest alphas.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), ind_zscore( sumrank( winsor( ratio( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), vol( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 5 ) ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( oancf, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RawShockAgainstCashFlowNews
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The same two-news interaction should work with the financing swing expressed in economic magnitude, dollars per unit of assets, which is the representation that has delivered both the largest alpha and the strongest Fama-MacBeth slope in this family.
input_signals.reasoning: The asset-scaled change carries the archive's best joint record (alpha −3.8% at t −3.07 with fmb −2.28) while the volatility-standardized version trades slope for alpha reliability, so pairing each with the cash-flow-news leg isolates which representation benefits more from the operating-news dimension. Run alongside Signal 1, this pair identifies the best final configuration rather than assuming one.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), ind_zscore( sumrank( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( oancf, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ThreeLegSelfFundingBreakdown
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), 1), SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), VOL(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 5)), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm's loss of self-funding is best measured by three complementary readings: the dollar size of its financing swing, how surprising that swing is relative to its own history, and whether internal cash generation is simultaneously deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: The two financing representations disagree about which firms are extreme — large swings at habitually active firms rank high on magnitude and low on surprise — and adding the operating-news leg supplies information from a different accounting statement altogether, so the three-way rank average should have the lowest measurement error of any archive construction. The risk, visible in generation 8's two-representation test, is dilution, which is why this is proposed alongside the cleaner two-leg versions rather than instead of them.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), ind_zscore( sumrank( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ), sumrank( winsor( ratio( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), vol( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 5 ) ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( oancf, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OutlierTrimmedFinancingNewsAmongProfitable
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0.5), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dltr)), at), 1), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cross-sectional slope of the winning signal is held down by a handful of merger- and recapitalization-driven financing swings; trimming at the fifth percentile should leave the portfolio sort essentially intact while making the pooled regression coefficient representative of typical firms.
input_signals.reasoning: Every attempt to raise fmb_tstat by re-weighting the gate or standardizing the shock has failed, leaving tail treatment as the one untested lever, and heavier winsorization is exactly the intervention that separates decile membership (unaffected by monotone trimming) from slope magnitude (highly sensitive to tails). If the alpha holds near −3% while the slope moves toward −3, this becomes the best-balanced signal in the archive on both forms of evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0.5 ), winsor( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dvt ), dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 5 ) )
